transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marc Rivera (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (CTO, Argo Health), Carlos Mendez (Platform Lead), Priya Shah (Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
Redwood AE/SE ran a live demo of rate limiting, quotas, and multi-tenant controls focusing on org/project API keys, per-project quotas, and per-org rate limiting. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated; security concerns (KMS, SSO, audit logs) discussed. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/security pack, pricing, and schedule a POC benchmark.

Topics covered:
- Org vs project API keys and best practices for multi-tenant isolation
- Rate limiting and quota enforcement (per-project, per-org, global)
- Console walkthrough: policy creation, usage dashboards, alerts
- Programmatic controls: API headers, key rotation, SDK behavior
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, data retention

Action items (auto): see metadata action_items above

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: alright everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off in a sec, i'm Lena from Redwood, AE on this account, Marc is our SE, we'll run through rate limits, org and project keys, and then go into a short console demo.
[00:18] Marc: hi all, hey thanks for having us. quick note, if chat audio cuts out pls flag; sometimes the transcriber writes KV cash instead of KV cache, so apologies in advance for weird words.
[00:30] Nina: thanks Lena, appreciate it. our main goal today is to understand how we can limit noisy tenants and also rotate keys per project, we run multi-tenant APIs across teams and need clear isolation.
[00:43] Carlos: also curious about burst behavior, like if a single project spikes, can we protect org-level capacity without breaking other teams?
[00:50] Marc: absolutely, that's the day-to-day we aimed for. ok, quick slide — org-level vs project-level keys. org keys are long-lived, used for billing and cross-project admin; project keys scoped to a single product or team.
[01:10] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[01:15] Marc: so on the Redwood platform you can set quotas two ways: quota units (token or request based) and rate limits (rps / tokens per minute). we often show a multi-tier policy: per-project soft quota with throttling and an org hard quota that can block or route to a lower-cost model.
[01:40] Nina: when you say route to lower-cost model, do you mean automatic fallback? what if that's unacceptable for PHI-sensitive workloads?
[01:48] Marc: good question — fallbacks are policy driven. for PHI we usually recommend dedicated isolated capacity or private deployment; the platform can be configured to never fallback to hosted model variants for those orgs.
[02:05] Priya: how does key rotation work with existing long-lived tokens? we need to rotate keys regularly and keep audit trails.
[02:12] Marc: keys support rolling rotation; you can create a new project key, flip traffic, and revoke old key. the console also shows rotation history and who rotated. audit logs are exportable to S3 or our log retention for up to your plan's retention window. (note: some customers call it "log retention" in calls, sometimes spelled retenion)
[02:36] Carlos: does the audit log include the token id only or full request footprints?
[02:42] Marc: by default we log metadata (token id, project id, model type, latency, token counts). payload-level logging is opt-in and always treated as sensitive; for PHI you'd turn payload logging off and instead use metrics-only mode.
[02:59] [03:00] Marc: ok switching to console demo — i'll share my screen. (screen share)
[03:10] Marc: here's the org admin page, you can see org-level quotas, billing thresholds, and a list of projects. i'll click into "Argo Health - dev" project.
[03:22] Marc: note the project has a project key shown as masked; you can create a new key, set TTL, and tag it with owners. tags feed into policies so you can do tag-based overrides.
[03:36] Carlos: can we create keys that only allow embeddings vs chat or generation?
[03:40] Marc: yes, we have granular scopes — endpoint scopes like embeddings, completions, or tools. you can create a key limited to embeddings and set egress controls.
[03:50] Nina: we're also interested in quotas by environment, e.g., dev vs prod separate budgets. can we enforce monthly quotas per project and per environment?
[03:59] Marc: yep, you can use project tags like "env:prod" and then create a quota policy that references the tag. so prod projects could have stricter quotas.
[04:10] [04:15] Marc: now on rate limits panel — this is where you set per-second and per-minute windows. you can set a bursting allowance; e.g., set rps 50 with burst 200 for short spikes, and longer-term rate smoothing.
[04:30] Priya: and how does this interact with batching? if we send batched requests via our SDK, do you count per-request or per-token?
[04:38] Marc: we count both dimensions. quota units can be configured as token-units or request-units. for most enterprise customers we recommend token-based quotas to better reflect cost. note: SDKs attempt to preserve efficient batching and annotate footprints.
[04:52] [05:00] Lena: quick commercial question — are there soft alerts before you hit an org quota? we want to notify product teams before enforcement kicks in.
[05:07] Marc: yes, alerting integrates with our console and can push to webhook, slack, or pagerduty. you can create thresholds at 70/85/95% and include runbooks.
[05:18] Carlos: is this configurable per-project or per-org?
[05:22] Marc: both. you can have project-level alerts plus org umbrella alerts.
[05:30] Nina: what about cross-org sharing — sometimes we have a shared data-team project that should not be constrained by product teams. can we create exempted project roles?
[05:39] Marc: you can create policy exceptions using role-based policies; exempted service accounts can be put on an allowlist. policies are evaluated in order so you can bump those higher.
[05:49] [06:00] Marc: i'll demo a policy creation — click "New Policy". name: "Prod strict quota". scope: tag env:prod. enforcement: hard block at 10M tokens/month, soft throttle at 9M tokens. action: block + notify org admins.
[06:20] Marc: see here in UI we can simulate policy with sample traffic, it shows projected enforcement and how many requests would be blocked. this helps you avoid surprises on rollout.
[06:34] Priya: that's helpful. does the simulator account for existing KV cache hits or cached prefixes? our billing model heavily uses prefix caching.
[06:44] Marc: the simulator can be set to include cache-hit ratio; default is 0.3 but you can provide a custom hit-rate to get better projections. (note: sometimes transcriber shows KV "cash" but the intention is KV cache)
[07:00] [07:15] Carlos: on the API side, what headers should our services set to identify project and tenant? we use a proxy that injects headers.
[07:22] Marc: recommended header is x-redwood-project-id and x-redwood-org-id, and you should also set x-redwood-call-context for multi-call tracing. the SDKs add these automatically if using per-project keys.
[07:36] Nina: can attackers spoof headers if they have a project key?
[07:40] Marc: headers are advisory; the real auth is the API key. headers are read for routing/observability. if using org-scoped keys, they are validated server-side. you can also restrict keys to IP allowlists and VPC egress ranges.
[07:55] [08:00] Priya: what KMS integrations do you support? we use HashiCorp Vault and Azure Key Vault.
[08:06] Marc: we have integrations with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM via our private deployment; HashiCorp Vault can be used via an on-prem connector. for Redwood-hosted keys we offer envelope encryption and customer-managed keys on enterprise plans.
[08:24] Nina: do you provide a proof or attestation that private keys are rotated?
[08:29] Marc: rotation events are logged in audit trail with user id and timestamp; we can produce exportable reports for audits.
[08:37] [08:50] Lena: segue to quotas in API: the API returns standard headers with remaining_quota and reset_time?
[08:58] Marc: yes we return x-rd-quota-remaining, x-rd-quota-reset, and x-rd-rate-limit; SDKs surface these as properties to let you implement client-side backoff. note sometimes the header names show differently in older SDK versions.
[09:20] Carlos: do you support per-route limits? e.g., embeddings endpoint has different capacity than chat models.
[09:27] Marc: yes, policy rules can match on route or model family. you can set separate quotas for embeddings vs chat.
[09:34] [10:00] Marc: i'll show an example policy attached to a project: open project -> policies -> usage. see the list, here's an embeddings-only cap for our "data-team" project.
[10:12] Marc: also note the platform allows "safety windows" where certain endpoints are only allowed during certain times, useful for batch jobs.
[10:22] Priya: interesting — we run nightly batch embedding jobs that we want to run outside business hours to reduce interference. can we whitelist those jobs?
[10:30] Marc: yes you can create time-windowed exceptions or use a deploy key that only works on a schedule.
[10:38] [11:00] Nina: on the dedicated vs hosted question — if we choose Redwood dedicated, do these quota controls still apply? is enforcement local to our pool?
[11:10] Marc: yes, Dedicated keeps the same control plane and policy model; enforcement happens at the runtime layer in your dedicated pool. you still get consolidated billing and org-level dashboards.
[11:22] Carlos: any differences in telemetry fidelity between hosted and private?
[11:27] Marc: private deployments can keep logs in your VPC and you can configure higher retention; hosted has built-in analytics with retention windows based on plan.
[11:36] [12:00] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[12:05] Marc: moving on — demo of key rotation API. i'll open the API docs page, endpoint POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/keys/rotate — simple body to create new key and set keep_old_days param.
[12:22] Marc: here's a sample curl, you'll see we include x-redwood-org-id header and Authorization bearer. the response contains new_key_id and masked_key.
[12:33] Carlos: can rotation be automated with a webhook callback when the new key is active?
[12:38] Marc: yes you can attach a webhook to rotation events; we also support an event bus export to your cloud.
[12:45] Priya: what about HSM-backed key material on Private? can we do in-place rotation with HSM?
[12:52] Marc: with our Private deployment and HSM integration you can issue rotate commands that trigger KMS-managed key rotation; the key material never leaves HSM.
[13:05] [13:15] Lena: commercial question — pricing model when using org quotas and fair-use? is there an overage rate?
[13:22] Marc: pricing is per-token with tiered discounts. for committed Dedicated you get reserved throughput; for hosted we have overage rates and soft-burst protections. we'll share the pricing sheet after the call.
[13:35] Nina: do you offer spend caps? we need to enforce company-level spending limits.
[13:40] Marc: you can set spend caps at org level; enforcement can either block or send alerts and throttle.
[13:48] [14:00] Carlos: are there RBAC roles tied to quota management? we want only infra admins to change quotas.
[14:06] Marc: yes RBAC is granular: Org Admin, Billing Admin, Project Owner, Read-only. quota and policy changes require Org Admin or specific policy manager roles.
[14:17] Priya: do you support SSO/SAML federation for our org?
[14:21] Lena: yes SSO with SAML and SCIM for user provisioning is supported on enterprise plans. sometimes the transcriber writes SMAL but it's SAML.
[14:32] [15:00] Marc: showing the Alerts page now — you can create an alert rule tied to a policy so when a project hits a threshold it pings slack. here's a sample webhook config.
[15:12] Marc: also you can link alerts to runbooks in the UI so on-call gets the exact steps.
[15:22] Carlos: sweet. on enforcement, is there a way to queue requests and drain them later or are blocked requests immediately rejected?
[15:30] Marc: for hard blocks it's an immediate 429. for throttles you get 202 accepted with a retry-after or the SDK will perform exponential backoff. we also offer request queuing in Dedicated setups for short spikes.
[15:46] [16:00] Nina: can we get a per-route SLA? some teams need <100ms p95 for short prompts.
[16:06] Marc: SLA commitments are possible on Dedicated and some enterprise Hosted plans — we can map per-route latency targets, but that typically requires reserved capacity.
[16:18] Lena: (note) there was a benchmark we ran with Nvidia where the 95th p99 was X ms — we'll include that benchmark link.
[16:28] [17:00] Marc: demo: show usage insights — tokens by project, top callers, anomaly detection. you can pin dashboards. the anomaly detector will flag sudden token spikes and create a ticket.
[17:40] Priya: does anomaly detection access payloads?
[17:44] Marc: no payloads; detection uses metrics and metadata only.
[17:50] [18:00] Carlos: technical deep dive: how do you evaluate a token for quota when using streaming? is it per-chunk?
[18:07] Marc: streaming counts are based on generated tokens; partial answers are accounted as they are committed to the KV cache and final tokenization. there are edge cases with streaming chunking but we have smoothing heuristics.
[18:24] Nina: ok good. any gotchas for us moving from a monolithic key to per-project keys?
[18:30] Marc: main work is rotating clients to send project id headers / use project keys; we provide migration helpers, middleware examples, and a compatibility mode where old org key still authenticates but is mapped to project for observability.
[18:46] [19:00] Marc: i'll show the middleware snippet — node/py examples. (snippets shown)
[19:12] Carlos: would like the python example. can you drop that in the repo or share a link?
[19:16] Marc: yes we'll share.
[19:20] [20:00] Priya: security — are data in transit and at rest encrypted?
[20:05] Marc: yes TLS in transit, data at rest encrypted; for customer-managed keys we support CMEK and HSM for private deployments.
[20:16] Nina: do you have published pen-test results or external attestations?
[20:21] Lena: we have SOC2 Type II and pen test summaries we can share under NDA.
[20:30] [21:00] Carlos: from an ops perspective, how fast can we react to a tenant causing problems — can we throttle that project immediately?
[21:07] Marc: yes in the console you can disable a project's key which immediately blocks requests; you can also flip policy to a stricter enforcement in seconds.
[21:18] [22:00] Marc: walking through an example: disabling key now (demo) — request returns 401 once disabled. re-enable within the console to restore.
[22:25] Carlos: perfect.
[22:30] [23:00] Nina: any integrations with IAM like Okta or GCP IAM?
[23:06] Marc: SSO via Okta yes, SCIM provisioning supported. for GCP IAM we have connectors for service accounts in private deployments.
[23:20] [24:00] Lena: okay wrapping up demo portion. recap of ask: Argo wants isolation, spend control, and rotation automation — all supported.
[24:12] Nina: yeah this looks promising. we're leaning Dedicated for PHI and isolated capacity but want to test hosted for less-sensitive workloads.
[24:22] Marc: sounds good. next steps: we'll send SOC2/security pack, pricing, and a POC runbook.
[24:32] Priya: can we get a sample key rotation script for Vault?
[24:36] Marc: yes i'll include a Vault example.
[24:40] [25:00] Carlos: timeline: we're targeting a POC in early March; we'll confirm internal buy-in.
[25:10] Lena: great — we'll follow up w/ dates.
[25:18] [26:00] Speaker 1: (background)
[26:05] Marc: quick Q from me: can you share approximate monthly token volume per environment? helps us size the POC.
[26:15] Carlos: rough numbers — prod ~15M tokens/month, staging ~4M, dev ~500k.
[26:25] Marc: ok good — that fits within our Dedicated small pool for testing.
[26:30] Nina: any legal requirements around data residency? we operate in EU and US and some records are required to stay in region.
[26:40] Marc: we support region pins and you can restrict traffic to specific data centers; for Private we can deploy entirely in your VPC region.
[26:52] [28:00] Priya: final security question — do you offer per-key IP allowlists?
[28:06] Marc: yes per-key allowlists are supported along with VPC egress enforcement.
[28:12] [29:00] Lena: ok, wrapping — quick recap and owners. Lena will send SOC2 and pricing, Marc will send POC runbook and code samples, Carlos to confirm POC date.
[29:20] Nina: thanks team.
[29:25] Carlos: thanks everyone.
[29:30] Marc: thanks all, happy to follow up.
[29:35] [30:00] (call ends)

Notes about transcript quality: there are a few transcription errors typical of Fireflies exports: K V cache sometimes spelled KV cash, SAML sometimes SMAL, and a few punctuation runs. But content reflects live demo flow and next steps.
